name: Curiosity
definition: Within the Communication domain, Curiosity is the Developmental Competency of asking thoughtful questions and exploring the other person's values, experiences, preferences, and perspectives with genuine interest and without rushing to conclusions. It is one of the phase-specific abilities required to complete the developmental task of Discernment within the Exploration phase.
healthy_markers: Asks thoughtful questions to understand the other person.
Explores values, experiences, preferences, and perspectives without rushing conclusions.
Shows genuine interest through follow-up questions and engaged responses.
common_challenges: Internal barriers such as fear, avoidance, unexamined relational schemas, or emotional dysregulation that inhibit Curiosity
relational barriers such as an unsafe, unresponsive, or undermining relational environment
environmental barriers such as stress load, time scarcity, or contextual instability. Barriers should be assessed when Curiosity remains incompletely developed despite intervention.

purpose: Curiosity enables the individual or relational system to meet the communication demands of Exploration, a phase in which individuals are gathering evidence about compatibility, character, and relational fit. The competency supports evaluating compatibility and gathering behavioral evidence before deeper relational investment.
